models_evaluated: RaySearch RayStation 3D U-net deep learning auto-segmentation

links.outcome: Contouring time with auto-segmentation plus correction versus manual delineation on same patients
links.effect: Time reduction in 95% of cases; mean 42.4% ± 26.5% for OARs and 58.5% ± 19.1% for CTVs; absolute mean reduction 00:08:51 and 00:25:38.
links.quote: Only for one patient case out of 20, the time needed to correct the OARs took more time than the manual delineation (00:12:40 vs 00:10:15), leading to a decrease in time in 95% of the patients.

links.outcome: Clinician qualitative scoring of AI contours as clinically acceptable, with or without corrections
links.effect: 92% of auto-contours were scored clinically acceptable with or without correction; CTVp unusable in seven cases, CTVn1 in six, CTVn4 in four.
links.quote: During qualitative measurements, the auto-contours got scored as clinical acceptable, with or without corrections, in 92% of the cases.

models_evaluated: 3D U-net left-sided breast cancer auto-segmentation model
3D U-net right-sided breast cancer auto-segmentation model

links.effect: Mean time reduction was 42.4% ± 26.5% for OARs and 58.5% ± 19.1% for CTVs.
links.quote: The time reduction (mean ± std) was 42.4% ± 26.5% and 58.5% ± 19.1% for OARs and CTVs, respectively, corresponding to an absolute mean reduction (hh:mm:ss) of 00:08:51 and 00:25:38.

links.effect: Right-sided CTVp mean DSC before correction was 0.92 ± 0.06; correction improved it by 0.02 ± 0.05.
links.quote: Good quantitative results were achieved before correction, e.g. mean DSC for the right-sided CTVp was 0.92 ± 0.06, whereas correction statistically significantly improved this contour by only 0.02 ± 0.05, respectively.

links.effect: Primary time-efficiency endpoint met: time reduction was achieved in 95% of cases including corrections.
links.quote: In 95% of the cases, time reduction was achieved while including corrections of the contours when needed.

links.effect: Auto-contours were scored clinically acceptable, with or without corrections, in 92% of cases.
links.quote: During qualitative measurements, the auto-contours got scored as clinical acceptable, with or without corrections, in 92% of the cases.

links.effect: CTVp, CTVn1, and CTVn4 were not usable in 7, 6, and 4 cases, respectively.
links.quote: The CTVp was found not to be usable in a total of seven cases, CTVn1 in six cases and CTVn4 in four cases.

links.outcome: impact of manual corrections on contour accuracy
links.effect: corrections significantly improved left CTVn1 across all metrics, but overall only a small number of cases had significantly different contours after correction (right CTVp DSC improved by 0.02 +/- 0.05)
links.quote: These results indicate that, although corrections were made in most of the cases, only for a small number of cases these corrections were actually significantly different.
